1401.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which may reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** Six places still format a timestamp with the machine's locale instead of the interface language: they call `toLocaleString()` / `toLocaleTimeString()` with no argument. In a Chinese interface on an English-locale machine the artifact version menu, the approval card, the model list and every `已保存 · <time>` line print `11/25/2026, 10:31:05 PM` inside otherwise Chinese text, while the rest of the app formats the same kind of value through `TEXT.languageTag`.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Set the interface to Chinese (`设置 › 通用 › 界面语言`) on a machine whose OS locale is `en-US`.
2. Open a report's artifact dialog and its version menu → each entry reads `v5 · 11/25/2026, 10:31:05 PM`.
3. Or approve a pending shell request → `请求时间` renders the same way.
4. Or change any settings value → the saved line reads `已保存 · 10:31:05 PM`.

**Observed** (`645dc7ba`)

```ts
// apps/desktop/src/views/ArtifactDialog.tsx:411
const when = new Date(candidate.createdAt).toLocaleString();
// apps/desktop/src/views/PermissionCard.tsx:75
<dd>{new Date(request.createdAt).toLocaleString()}</dd>
// apps/desktop/src/views/settings/ModelSettings.tsx:487
{list ? ` · ${new Date(list.fetchedAt).toLocaleString()}` : ""}
// apps/desktop/src/views/settings/setting-controls.tsx:34   (also Timeouts.tsx:91, MemorySettings.tsx:53)
setSavedAt(new Date().toLocaleTimeString());
```

`Date#toLocaleString` with no argument resolves to the host locale, so the output follows the operating system, not the language chosen in the app.

**Contrast.** The same app already has the right call shape in four places, which is what makes this look like an oversight rather than a decision:

```ts
// apps/desktop/src/views/Sidebar.tsx:91
new Date(time).toLocaleTimeString(TEXT.languageTag, { hour: "2-digit", minute: "2-digit" })
// apps/desktop/src/views/MemoryCardDialog.tsx:108
date.toLocaleTimeString(TEXT.languageTag, { hour: "2-digit", minute: "2-digit" })
```

**Root cause.** The locale argument was simply omitted at these call sites. There is no shared "format this timestamp for the interface" helper, so each call site decides on its own and six of them forgot.

**Expected.** Every user-facing timestamp goes through `TEXT.languageTag` (plus a fixed option set where the shape matters, as `Sidebar` and `MemoryCardDialog` do). A small `formatStamp(iso)` / `formatClock(date)` pair next to `TEXT` would keep the next call site from picking the default again.

**Impact**

- One screen mixes two date formats: `v5 · 11/25/2026, 10:31:05 PM` next to a Chinese hint and a Chinese session title; it reads as a half-finished localization, which is exactly how users judge the whole page.
- `已保存 · 10:31:05 PM` is the *only* feedback a settings write gives (the `WriteStatus` line), and `Timeouts` writes on every field blur — so the most frequently shown string in 设置 is the one in the wrong format.
- The approval card's `请求时间` is what a user reads to decide whether a stale request is still theirs; `11/25/2026` vs `2026/11/25` is a real misread risk at a security decision.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client, source `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a`.
- Derived from the six call sites above; not reproduced in a running client (the test host was unavailable at the time). The OS-locale dependency is documented browser behaviour: the locale argument omitted means "the host's default locale".

### Additional Information

- `apps/desktop/src/views/AccountPage.tsx` was reported separately for hardcoding `zh-CN` the other way around; this issue is the mirror case (no locale at all), and the two fixes are complementary: pick the interface language in both.
- The settings write feedback path is `WriteStatus` (`setting-controls.tsx:47-62`), which prints `state.savedAt` verbatim, so fixing the three producers fixes every page that shows it.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a` (main, 2026-11-25).

1402.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which may reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** `设置 › 超时` lets the reader set `一轮对话` shorter than `网关空闲`, a combination the service refuses. Nothing on the page says the two are ordered, so the write comes back as a raw sentence naming `gatewayTurnTimeoutMs`, and because the page PUTs the whole object it silently reverts every field to the last stored value — including edits that had nothing to do with the refused one.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `设置 › 超时`, set `网关空闲` to `120` and `一轮对话` to `30` seconds.
2. Leave the field (the page writes on blur, no 保存 button).
3. Repeat with a second field edited in between, e.g. `执行超时` → `10`, then set `一轮对话` below `网关空闲`.

**Observed** (`645dc7ba`)

```tsx
// apps/desktop/src/views/settings/Timeouts.tsx:80-106
try {
  await updateTimeoutSettings(client, next);      // whole-object PUT
  ...
} catch (reason) {
  queued.current = undefined;
  update(stored.current ?? next);                 // every field back to the stored value
  setFailure(reason instanceof Error ? reason.message : TEXT.settings.saveFailed);
  return;
}
```

The service's rule (the only place it exists):

```ts
// services/api/src/store/settings.ts (normalizeTimeoutSettings)
if (result.gatewayIdleTimeoutMs > 0 && result.gatewayTurnTimeoutMs > 0
  && result.gatewayTurnTimeoutMs < result.gatewayIdleTimeoutMs) {
  throw new Error("gatewayTurnTimeoutMs must be greater than or equal to gatewayIdleTimeoutMs when both timeouts are finite");
}
```

The two hints the page shows say nothing about it:

```ts
// apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:1839,1841
gatewayIdleHint: "连接一直没有新数据时等待的时间。",
gatewayTurnHint: "一轮对话允许的最长时间。",
```

**Root cause.** The ordering rule is enforced only by the store, and the page neither states it nor checks it before committing; the failure handler then treats any rejection as "the whole draft is wrong" and restores the last stored object.

**Expected.** The hint for `一轮对话` states that it cannot be shorter than the idle timeout while both are finite (the service's own catalogue already words it that way: `When both are set, the turn limit is at least the idle limit`), the page refuses the combination at the field and marks it, and a rejected write does not revert fields the user did not change.

**Impact**

- The edit visibly undoes itself: the numbers snap back to what they were, so it reads as "the page did not save" rather than "that value is not allowed" — and the only explanation is an English sentence quoting internal field names.
- The revert is not scoped to the offending field: `update(stored.current ?? next)` restores the entire last-confirmed object, so a legitimate change made in the same draft (say `执行超时`) is thrown away without a word.
- With unlimited (`不限`) involved the rule disappears (`0` means no limit), so the same pair is accepted or refused depending on an unrelated switch — again with nothing on screen to explain it.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client, source `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a`.
- Derived from `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/system/Timeouts.tsx:27-36, 80-122` and `services/api/src/store/settings.ts` (`normalizeTimeoutSettings`); not reproduced in a running client (the test host was unavailable at the time).

### Additional Information

- The wording/localization half of this (an English server sentence reaching a Chinese UI) is the same family as the reported `Runner` alias validation; the defect here is the missing rule on the form plus the unscoped revert, so the fix is the hint, the field check and a revert limited to the refused field — not the translation.
- `services/api/src/configuration/system-adapters.ts:95` already documents the intended wording for this field ("When both are set, the turn limit is at least the idle limit"), so the text exists on the server side and simply never reached the client hint.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a` (main, 2026-11-25).

1403.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding technical details and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which may reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** In `设置 › Idea Tree`, the `最大深度` and `最大节点` boxes cannot be cleared and rewrite what is typed into them: every keystroke is parsed and normalised immediately, and a keystroke that does not already parse as a valid number is dropped instead of being kept as a draft. The `最大 token` box right below them behaves differently, so the same form has two editing behaviours.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `设置 › 智能 › Idea Tree` while a research has values (e.g. `最大深度` = `4`, `最大节点` = `20`).
2. Click at the end of `最大深度`, press `Backspace`.
3. Also try `最大 token`: click at the end, press `Backspace` (or select all and delete).

**Observed** (`645dc7ba`)

```tsx
// apps/desktop/src/views/settings/IdeaTreeSettings.tsx:57-61
function readNumber(raw: string): number | undefined {
  if (raw.trim() === "") return undefined;
  const value = Number(raw);
  return Number.isFinite(value) && value >= 0 ? value : undefined;
}
// :146-153  and  :155-163
onChange={(event) => { const value = readNumber(event.target.value); if (value !== undefined) patch({ maxDepth: value }); }}
value={number(draft.maxDepth)}
```

`Backspace` produces `""`, `readNumber("")` is `undefined`, no `patch` happens, and the controlled input re-renders with the old number — the digit comes straight back. Typing a `-` first (to reach `0`, or just before noticing it is not allowed) is dropped the same way, as is `1.`.

By contrast the token box takes the empty state explicitly, which is why clearing that one works:

```tsx
// :170
onChange={(event) => patch({ maxTokens: readNumber(event.target.value) ?? null })}
```

**Root cause.** The two boxes have no draft: the JSX value is the parsed model value, and the change handler only writes to the model when the text already parses. Any intermediate text (empty, `-`, `1.`) is therefore rejected at the keystroke that created it, and the field snaps back.

**Expected.** All three boxes edit as text and commit on blur (the shape `SettingsNumber` in `views/settings/setting-controls.tsx` already implements for 配额 and 数量), or at least keep the raw text while the field is focused. Empty should be allowed while typing and then either refused or restored on blur with a visible mark.

**Impact**

- Clearing a field is impossible, which is the normal first move when replacing a value; the reader has to select-all (`Ctrl+A`) instead, and a user who does not do that concludes the box is read-only.
- The value under the caret is replaced by the old one, so a mistyped digit cannot be corrected by deleting it — the only fix is to retype the whole number from a selection.
- The form is inconsistent with itself one row apart (`最大 token` clears, the other two do not), which reads as a broken field rather than a rule.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client, source `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a`.
- Derived from `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/IdeaTreeSettings.tsx:55-61, 145-175`; not reproduced in a running client (the test host was unavailable at the time).

### Additional Information

- This is deliberately separate from the value-meaning report against the same page (`readNumber` collapsing "empty" and "invalid" into one `undefined`, which makes `-5` mean "no cap"): that one is about what a stored value means, this one is about the field refusing to be edited. A draft-based field plus an explicit "empty = null" call site fixes both, but they fail differently and are worth their own checks.
- `SettingsNumber` (`setting-controls.tsx:65-96`) is the ready-made pattern: local draft, `onCommit` on blur/Enter, `aria-invalid` plus a message when the committed text does not parse.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a` (main, 2026-11-25).

### Checklist - [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help. - [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version. - [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding technical details and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which may reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed. ### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem **Summary.** The Evolve runtime is polled only until it answers `ready`, and never again — not on a timer, not when the setup dialog opens, and the `refreshStatus()` helper that would do it is never called by anyone. So an app that saw `ready` keeps saying `ready` after the sidecar has died: the "runtime cannot run a search" banner stays hidden, `开始设计` stays enabled, and the user only finds out after paying for a whole design turn. **Steps to reproduce** 1. Start the app with the Evolve sidecar running (`/api/evolve/status` → `ready`) so the first poll settles. 2. Stop or crash `sd-evolve` (or lose the sidecar, as a restarted deployment does). 3. Open `新建程序演进实验` and press `开始设计`. **Observed** (`645dc7ba`) ```ts // apps/desktop/src/evolve/use-evolve.ts:88-96 const load = () => { void getEvolveStatus(client) .then((next) => { if (!live) return; setStatus(next); if (next.state !== "ready") timer = setTimeout(load, STATUS_POLL_MS); // stops on ready }) ``` The dialog trusts that value for both the warning and the gate: ```tsx // apps/desktop/src/views/evolve/EvolveCreateDialog.tsx:184,197,260 const ready = status.state === "ready"; const canSend = ready && blocked === undefined && goal.trim() !== ""; {ready ? null :
…
} ``` And the one hook that could re-read it is unused: ```ts // evolve/use-evolve.ts:177 — exposed on the handle const refreshStatus = useCallback(async () => { … }, [client]); // grep: `refreshStatus` appears only in this file (declaration + the handle's return) ``` `refresh()` (which also re-runs the status effect) is called only around run activity — `App.tsx:440-443` while a design is awaited, `:480` after a run was created, `:1686` on run change — and **not** when the dialog opens (`setEvolveCreate` at `:1293` / `:1486`). **Root cause.** Readiness is treated as a one-way latch: the poll exists only to watch an *installing* runtime become ready, and nothing watches a ready runtime become unavailable. The dialog's own contract says the banner is "the first thing to know" before a search is attempted, which only holds if the value is fresh at the moment the dialog opens. **Expected.** A cheap re-read when `新建程序演进实验` opens (`refreshStatus()` is already there), or a slow poll while the app is visible (30–60 s, on top of the existing 4 s poll while not ready). A stale `ready` should never be able to hide the warning. **Impact** - The user pays for a design conversation (measured turns on this project: 68K, 135K, 260K, 791K tokens) and only then gets a failure, because `create_evolve_run` cannot reach the sidecar. - Nothing in the UI connects the failure to the runtime: the dialog said 就绪 moments earlier, so the natural conclusion is that the goal or the model is at fault. - The same staleness is what makes the `D5` check "runtime ready ⇒ banner hidden" pass while the service is actually down; a test that reads the banner gets the opposite of the truth. - The `error` state is equally sticky in the other direction: a runtime that was unreachable at startup keeps the dialog on the install banner until some run activity bumps `revision`, even after the sidecar is back. ### Detailed Environment Information Description - ScienceDiscovery desktop client, source `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a`. - Derived from `apps/desktop/src/evolve/use-evolve.ts:65-113,177-190` and `apps/desktop/src/views/evolve/EvolveCreateDialog.tsx:184-197,256-269`, plus the call sites of `refresh` in `App.tsx`; not reproduced in a running client (the test host was unavailable at the time). ### Additional Information - The runtime banner is the only place the app states the prerequisite; `设置 › 智能 › Idea Tree` answers the same 503 in its own pane, so a dead sidecar surfaces differently depending on which surface the user happens to open (that pane has its own once-at-mount read). - The design turn is the expensive step here, and the dialog exists precisely to avoid spending it on a setup that cannot run — so the fix is one request at open, not a new mechanism. ### Version Information - `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a` (main, 2026-11-25).

1412.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding technical details and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which may reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** When an Idea Tree research runs out of its token budget the engine records it as `paused` — the same status a user's pause produces — so the panel offers `继续`. Pressing it re-runs the research, which hits the same ceiling before doing any work and settles back to `已暂停`: the one recovery action on offer can never make progress.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `设置 › 智能 › Idea Tree` → set `token 上限` to a small value (e.g. `200000`) and save.
2. Start a research and let it run until the ceiling is reached.
3. In the task panel press `继续`.

**Observed** (`645dc7ba`)

```python
# services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py:329-332
budget = self.state['settings'].get('maxTokens')
if budget and self.state['tokens'] + self.state.get('unreportedBudgetEstimate', 0) + self.reserved + estimate > budget:
    raise BudgetReached('Remaining token budget cannot fund the next stage')
```

```python
# :736-737 — a spent budget settles as a pause, not as its own outcome
except BudgetReached as error:
    s.update(status='paused', reason=str(error))
```

The desktop treats `paused` as resumable, so the button appears:

```tsx
// apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaResearchPanel.tsx:151
const canResume = research.status === "paused" || research.status === "interrupted";
```

and the API's `continue` accepts it:

```ts
// services/api/src/idea-tree/research.ts:33
if (previous && !["paused", "interrupted"].includes(previous.research.status)) throw new Error("Research is not resumable");
```

`continue` → `start()` → `run()` → the first stage's budget check raises `BudgetReached` again (the reason string has not changed and `tokens` cannot go down), so the research is `paused` again with the same reason. Only `结束` leaves the state.

**Root cause.** "Ran out of budget" is mapped onto the user-facing status `paused`, and nothing downstream can tell the two apart: the desktop's `canResume` sees a pause, the API's resumability check sees a pause, and `run()` has no notion of a terminal budget outcome. Evolve runs in the same product do have their own terminal status (`budget_exhausted`), which is what makes the inconsistency visible.

**Expected.** Budget exhaustion should be its own terminal status (as `budget_exhausted` is for searches): the panel shows it as finished, offers no `继续`, and says how much of the cap was used. If resuming is meant to be possible, it needs a way to raise the cap first — a `继续` that cannot do anything is worse than no button.

**Impact**

- The button named as the recovery action is a no-op loop; a user watching the tree will press it repeatedly and conclude the feature is broken.
- The tree stops half-built with no way to complete it and no way to pick it up with a bigger budget; the spent tokens are lost.
- The only explanation on screen is the engine's English sentence (`Remaining token budget cannot fund the next stage`) — the panel's reason line is a placeholder that returns the string unchanged (`TEXT.ideaTree.reason: (reason: string) => reason`).

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Source `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a`; Desktop client + Evolve sidecar.
- Derived from `research.py:329-332,736-737`, `apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaResearchPanel.tsx:151-155`, `services/api/src/idea-tree/research.ts:31-34`; not reproduced in a running stack (the test host was unavailable at the time).

### Additional Information

- `maxTokens` defaults to `null` (no cap), so this needs the field to be set — it is a documented setting: `tokensHint: "单次研究可用的总 token；留空表示不额外限制。"`
- The same mapping makes a *restart* pause and a *budget* pause look identical apart from the reason text, which is not translated.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a` (main, 2026-11-25).

### Checklist - [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help. - [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version. - [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding technical details and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which may reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed. ### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem **Summary.** The Idea Tree card in the transcript cuts the research objective at 28 characters with **no ellipsis**, so a shortened title is indistinguishable from a complete one. The search card sitting in the same list truncates at 64 *columns* and appends `…`, so the two card types also disagree about how much of the goal they show. **Steps to reproduce** 1. Start an Idea Tree research with an objective longer than 28 characters (easy: "评估不同预处理工艺对水处理膜通量衰减的影响并给出最优参数组合"). 2. Look at the card at the foot of the answer. **Observed** (`645dc7ba`) ```tsx // apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaResearchCard.tsx:34-39 export function ideaCardTitle(objective: string): string { const line = objective.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim(); if (!line) return t.heading; return Array.from(line).slice(0, 28).join(""); // no "…", and 28 code points, not columns } ``` Compare the search card beside it: ```ts // apps/desktop/src/evolve/model.ts:335-350 const TITLE_COLUMNS = 64; … if (width > TITLE_COLUMNS) return `${out.trimEnd()}…`; // cuts on printed width, marks the cut ``` The full objective is only in the button's `title` attribute (`:106`), i.e. behind a hover. **Root cause.** The card has its own one-line rule instead of the one the search card already uses, and it counts characters rather than the width they print at — a CJK character takes two columns, so 28 CJK characters is ~56 columns while 28 Latin characters is ~28. No marker is added at the cut. **Expected.** Use the same rule as `evolveShortTitle` (64 columns, `…` at the cut), or at minimum append `…` when the string was shortened. **Impact** - The card is the only handle on a research in the transcript, and it silently claims the objective ends where it was cut — a reader who never hovers takes half a sentence for the task. - Two researches whose objectives share their first 28 characters become indistinguishable rows, which is exactly the case with a series of re-runs on the same topic. - The visible width jumps between the two card types in the same list (28 CJK characters for a research vs. 32 for a search), so a mixed list looks ragged and the shorter one looks like a complete title. ### Detailed Environment Information Description - Source `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a`; ScienceDiscovery desktop client. - Derived from `apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaResearchCard.tsx:34-39,103-120` and `apps/desktop/src/evolve/model.ts:321-350`; not reproduced in a running client (the test host was unavailable at the time). ### Additional Information - The panel header shows the objective in full (`IdeaResearchPanel.tsx:157

{research.objective}

`), so this only affects the transcript card. - The card's own doc comment says it shows "the objective's first line, folded to one short sentence" — the marker is what would make that folding visible. ### Version Information - `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a` (main, 2026-11-25).

1415.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which may reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** In `设置 › Idea Tree`, `最大深度` accepts values above `20` and `最大节点` accepts `1` or anything above `10 000`. The form shows no error and leaves `保存` enabled, and the value is only refused by the store after the click, as an English server sentence inside a Chinese pane. Neither field states a range, so nothing tells the reader that `20` is the cap.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `设置 › 智能 › Idea Tree`.
2. Type `50` into `最大深度`, or `1` into `最大节点`.
3. Press `保存`.

**Observed** (`644730f8`, after #1409)

```tsx
// apps/desktop/src/views/settings/IdeaTreeSettings.tsx:78-82
function parseCount(raw: string): number | undefined {
  if (raw.trim() === "") return undefined;
  const value = Number(raw);
  return Number.isSafeInteger(value) && value >= 1 ? value : undefined;   // no upper bound, nodes min is 1
}
// :197-233  the inputs carry min={1} and no max
```

```
// services/api/src/store/settings.ts:629-631, boundedInteger throws (:579-595)
maxDepth = boundedInteger(input.maxDepth, "maxDepth", 1, 20, current.maxDepth);
maxNodes = boundedInteger(input.maxNodes, "maxNodes", 2, 10_000, current.maxNodes);
```

The pane prints the thrown message verbatim (`IdeaTreeSettings.tsx:162-165`), so the reader gets `maxDepth must be between 1 and 20` / `maxNodes must be between 2 and 10000` only after pressing `保存`, in the middle of a Chinese form.

**Root cause.** The pane's own validation covers "is this a positive integer", not "is this an integer the store accepts", and the two inputs declare `min={1}` for both fields even though the store's node floor is `2`. The bounds exist elsewhere in the same app: the per-run control uses `min={1} max={20}` and `min={2} max={10000}` (`apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaTreeOverrideDialog.tsx:349-362`), and the shared `SettingsNumber` (`apps/desktop/src/views/settings/setting-controls.tsx:65-95`) validates min/max before committing.

**Expected.** The field refuses what the store refuses: depth `1..20`, nodes `2..10 000`, tokens `1..MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, with the accepted range named in the note (or in the hint) instead of "at least 1". Setting `max={20}` / `min={2} max={10000}` on the inputs would also let the browser say it.

**Impact**

- A reader who wants "a deeper tree" types `50`, sees no complaint, presses `保存`, and is told `maxDepth must be between 1 and 20` in English — the same "the failure surfaces at 保存 with a server message instead of at the field" shape this page was just fixed for `0`.

- Derived by reading `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/IdeaTreeSettings.tsx` and `services/api/src/store/settings.ts`; not reproduced in a running client.

### Additional Information

## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

On the desktop build, clicking the HUAWEI ID sign-in button does not open the HUAWEI login window. Instead the app goes straight back to the main page.

Root cause:

`apps/desktop/src/auth/account.ts` reads the account-service base URL from the Vite build variable `VITE_ACCOUNTS_API`:

```ts
export function accountsBaseUrl(): string {
  return buildEnv("VITE_ACCOUNTS_API").trim().replace(/\/+$/u, "");
}
```

`packages/account-session/src/index.ts` then builds the sign-in URL as:

```ts
return `${normalizedBase(options.baseUrl ?? "")}/v1/auth/huawei/start?${new URLSearchParams({ returnUrl }).toString()}`;
```

The repository ships no versioned default for `VITE_ACCOUNTS_API`: it only exists in `apps/desktop/.env.example`, with a comment telling users to copy it to a gitignored `.env.local`. On a fresh clone, `pnpm build` therefore bakes an empty value, and `huaweiSignInUrl()` produces a same-origin relative path `/v1/auth/huawei/start?returnUrl=...`.

The desktop UI runs on a local loopback origin (127.0.0.1:431x). In `services/api/src/http/index.ts`, every GET outside `/api/` is served by `serveStatic`, and `services/api/src/http/static.ts` falls back to `index.html` for any path that is not a file. The login navigation is therefore answered with the SPA itself. The app remounts with no `#auth-ticket` fragment and, because a local token already exists, skips the sign-in page and enters the main page directly.

Reproduction:

1. Clone the repository on Windows.
2. Run `pnpm --filter "@sciencediscovery/desktop" build` without creating `apps/desktop/.env.local`.
3. Launch the desktop app and click the HUAWEI ID sign-in button.
4. Observed: the app reloads into the main page and no HUAWEI login window is shown.

Expected:

A fresh clone should build a desktop sign-in flow that reaches the account service. The default value should be versioned in the repository (for example a committed `apps/desktop/.env`) rather than depending on a gitignored local file. A local override can still use `.env.local`.

Note: `apps/web` has the same `VITE_ACCOUNTS_API` contract, but the web dev server proxies `/v1` and the web production deployment serves account routes same-origin, so an empty value is intentional there. The desktop app has no `/v1` proxy and its UI origin is a local loopback address, so the empty default is broken for desktop.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

- OS: Windows 11
- Build command: `pnpm --filter "@sciencediscovery/desktop" build`
- Vite: 8.1.4
- Repository state: `main` (the same logic also exists on the current verification branch)
- No `apps/desktop/.env` or `apps/desktop/.env.local` present at build time

## Additional Information

Verified in the built bundle that `import.meta.env.VITE_ACCOUNTS_API` is compiled to an empty string, so the generated sign-in URL starts with `/v1/auth/huawei/start` instead of the deployed account-service origin.

## Version Information

- ScienceDiscovery: 0.4.0 (main)

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

The desktop subagent conversation displays internal audit metadata alongside the final `run_shell` result and repeats streamed output under the same Output heading. Users cannot tell which text is command output, progress, or the projected tool result sent to the model.

PR #717 introduced model-facing output projection, but the UI still renders `step.content`, `step.progress`, and pretty-printed `step.details` consecutively. The audit JSON includes execution/agent/runner/workspace IDs, timestamps, `[omitted]` placeholders, and `__detailsBoundary`. These implementation details are not useful in ordinary user-facing output.

**Minimal reproduction**

1. Have a subagent call `run_shell` with a short command such as:
   ```sh
   printf 'batch1 written\n'
   ```
2. Wait for completion and expand the tool step in the desktop subagent conversation.
3. When progress was captured, the same message appears in both the final stdout and progress. Audit details are also rendered under Output.

The equivalent minimal rendering input is a completed tool step with:

```json
{
  "kind": "tool",
  "status": "completed",
  "toolName": "run_shell",
  "content": "{\"state\":\"completed\",\"exitCode\":0}\nstdout:\nbatch1 written\nstderr:\n",
  "progress": "batch1 written\n",
  "details": {
    "stdout": "[omitted]",
    "stderr": "[omitted]",
    "agentId": "subagent:example",
    "runnerId": "local",
    "__detailsBoundary": { "omittedPayloadFields": true, "truncated": false }
  }
}
```

**Observed behavior**

A user-reported successful execution produced this sequence (identifiers shortened):

```text
{"executionId":"shell:example","state":"completed","exitCode":0,"createdFiles":["outputs/literature_sources.json"],"modifiedFiles":[],"recovery":{"schemaVersion":1,"capability":"unknown","reason":"NOT_REPORTED"}}
stdout:
batch1 written

stderr:
batch1 written
{
  "executionId": "shell:example",
  "state": "completed",
  "exitCode": 0,
  "stdout": "[omitted]",
  "stderr": "[omitted]",
  "agentId": "subagent:example",
  "runnerId": "local",
  "workspaceId": "ws_example",
  "__detailsBoundary": {
    "maxArrayItems": 100,
    "maxDepth": 8,
    "maxObjectKeys": 100,
    "maxStringChars": 4096,
    "maxTotalStringChars": 64000,
    "omittedPayloadFields": true,
    "truncated": false
  }
}
```

The second `batch1 written` is consistent with the UI rendering progress after the final result's empty `stderr:` section; it must not be interpreted as proof that the command wrote to stderr.

**Expected behavior**

- Ordinary tool output shows useful command output, completion/failure status, generated files, and actionable error or recovery guidance.
- Internal audit metadata is retained for diagnostics without being rendered in ordinary user-facing output, including inside an additional collapsed audit block.
- Progress can be shown during execution; completion uses the final result without repeating the same streamed text or making progress appear to be stderr.
- Default recovery metadata such as `unknown` / `NOT_REPORTED` and empty bookkeeping lists should not clutter ordinary user-facing output. Actionable recovery information must remain available.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Reported on 2026-11-26 with a successful local `run_shell` execution (`runnerId: local`, exit code 0) in a subagent.
- The desktop subagent renderer matches the reported output ordering. The reporter's exact app build, operating system, and Node version were not supplied.
- Upstream main was inspected remotely to confirm that the affected rendering path remains present. No application/browser journey was run for this report.
- The rendering reproduction is data-only and does not depend on external providers, scientific packages, or special hardware.

### Additional Information

Source on inspected upstream main:

- [Desktop StepBody renders content, progress, and audit details together](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/96763c10053ac4f008a42a59e5c2305f266ef0bd/apps/desktop/src/views/SubagentDetail.tsx#L75-L111).
- Related projection change: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/717.

This is a user-facing presentation issue. The model-facing result and audit metadata are separate: the JiuwenSwarm bridge returns `dispatched.content` to the model, while `details` is retained separately in tool events. The audit JSON visible here does not by itself indicate a model-facing projection failure. Preserve audit storage and actionable execution information when fixing the display.

### Version Information

- Inspected upstream main: `96763c10053ac4f008a42a59e5c2305f266ef0bd`.
- Related merged PR: #717, merge commit `c2cb3119b463c7de76772568d7b054150da0d8d7`.

﻿### Checklist

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** I followed [用 Idea Tree 探索水处理催化剂](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/zh/docs/domains/idea-tree-catalyst-design.html) ([docs/zh/domains/idea-tree-catalyst-design.md](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/main/docs/zh/domains/idea-tree-catalyst-design.md)) and left one session (`A`) running an Idea Tree exploration (`正在规划下一步`). I then opened a new session `B`, typed `/idea-tree-team 这是一个测试`, pressed Enter — the Idea Tree parameters card opened — and pressed `确认`, which by design sends nothing. Switching straight back to `A`, **`A`'s composer already contained `这是一个测试`**, without the token: a sentence that had only ever been typed in `B`.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Follow the tutorial: create a session and send `/idea-tree-team …`; let the agent start planning. Keep this session — call it `A` — open.
2. `新增会话` (welcome page, call it `B`).
3. Type `/idea-tree-team 这是一个测试` into `B`'s composer and press Enter; the Idea Tree parameters card opens.
4. Press `确认` (nothing is sent, as intended — `B` keeps the token and the sentence, screenshot 1).
5. Click `A` in the sidebar.
6. `A`'s composer holds `这是一个测试` (screenshot 2, red box), with no token, and nothing in `A`'s transcript ever contained that sentence. Pressing Enter there would send it into `A`.

**Observed**

- `B` after `确认`: the token `/idea-tree-team` plus `这是一个测试`, unsent.
- `A` (still running) after the switch: the same sentence, no token.

_Screenshots are attached at the end of this report — (1) the new session right after `确认`, (2) the previously running session after switching back._

**Why it happens.** The confirmed card's seed outlives the surface it was written for by exactly one render, and the composer of the session being opened adopts it:

- `确认` seeds instead of sending: `confirmIdeaSend` → `seedIdeaCommand` → `setSeededCommand({ command, nonce, text })` ([App.tsx:1343-1362](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/main/apps/desktop/src/App.tsx#L1343-L1362)). Nothing leaves the client, so the seed is all that carries the draft.
- The session switch clears that seed in an *effect*: `setSeededCommand(undefined)` inside the `[state.sessionId]` effect ([App.tsx:382-393](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/main/apps/desktop/src/App.tsx#L382-L393)). Effects run after the render, so the first render of the newly selected session still sees `B`'s seed.
- That render is exactly where the conversation composer mounts: the welcome page's composer unmounts and `<Composer {...composerProps} />` ([App.tsx:1676](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/main/apps/desktop/src/App.tsx#L1676)) starts from the seed it can still see — `useState(seededCommand?.text ?? "")` and `useState(seededCommand?.command)` ([Composer.tsx:933-938](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/main/apps/desktop/src/views/Composer.tsx#L933-L938)).
- The seed is cleared on the next effect pass, and the composer's own rule then drops only the token while keeping the sentence — deliberately, because "the sentence stays: it is the reader's" ([Composer.tsx:1079-1094](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/main/apps/desktop/src/views/Composer.tsx#L1079-L1094)). By then the sentence is not the reader's for *this* session: it was written in `B`.

So a seed created on the welcome page seeds the composer of whichever session is opened next. The same channel also lets a draft typed in one conversation survive into another: the composer at `App.tsx:1676` carries no `key`, so its `text` state is shared by every conversation the reader opens (the effect above is what removes the token, not the sentence).

**Expected**

- A seed belongs to the surface that created it. After `确认` in `B`, the token and the sentence stay in `B`; opening `A` shows `A`'s own draft — empty here.
- A session switch never moves a sentence between sessions, in either direction: the conversation composer is keyed by the session (e.g. `key={state.sessionId ?? landingKey(state)}`), or the draft is dropped as part of the switch, before the target session's composer mounts.
- `SeededCommand` should say which session (or draft) it was created for and be ignored by any composer showing a different one, so the effect-based clearing is no longer what keeps it from leaking.

**Impact.** The running session's composer now holds a sentence the reader never wrote there, in a place where Enter sends it (`/idea-tree-team` would then start a second, long and costly research — in the wrong session). It also contradicts the intent recorded in the code for #1277, where the card must not intercept the send: the sentence it was told to keep ends up in another session.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery client, Windows, 2026-11-15 build (as reported by the reporter).
- Reproduced from the tutorial page above, with one Idea Tree session left running while a second session was drafted.

### Additional Information

- Two screenshots above: the new session after `确认`, and the previously running session after switching back.
- Code references are `main` as of 2026-11-26; the behaviour is unchanged in the tree I read.
- Related: #1277 introduced the deferred card this seed feeds.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, client build of 2026-11-15; references read from `main` (2026-11-26).

![切回正在探索的会话：输入框出现新会话输入的 这是一个测试](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2876151-ffed-4ab1-b174-15e68e67d0b3)

### Checklist

- [x] The affected paths remain present in the latest upstream main inspected below.
- [x] Environment, observed evidence and a minimal cancellation reproduction are provided below.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

When a PUCT search exhausts its token budget, the control plane requests a normal stop. This loses the distinction between cancelling work and a candidate/model failing: in-flight calls can become “empty replies” / `candidate-failed`, and final held-out evaluation inherits the already-triggered stop callback and is reported as a failure of the best candidate.

**Observed on a Windows desktop run on 2026-11-26**

The run requested 32 expansions, 4 workers, 600,000 total tokens, 7,200 seconds, 96,000 tokens per model call and 180 seconds per candidate evaluation. It used `custom_script`, with 4 rollout / 8 gate / 4 test shards, `thinking: auto`, and recorded `thinkingEffort: high`.

- It ran for about 60 minutes. The tree contained the baseline and 23 candidates; 13 candidates had scores, including 3 with per-instance timeout penalties. Ten candidates had scores without evaluator errors.
- At 580,260 recorded tokens, work was still in flight. A later cost event reported 676,832 tokens; the run metadata ended with `status: budget_exhausted` and `error: token budget reached (600000)`.
- At shutdown, the service logged `completion abandoned: the run was stopped` three times. The event stream then recorded nodes 20–22 as `the model returned an empty reply`, and classified them as `candidate-failed`.
- Node 18 had generated code but its evaluation was cancelled with `the search was stopped`; it was also classified as `candidate-failed`.
- The final warning was `the best candidate failed on the test shards: the search was stopped`. No final held-out score/evidence was produced. This is an uncompleted evaluation, not evidence that the best program failed its tests.
- The terminal sidecar event said `status: stopped`, `stopReason: max_iters`, `expansionsPlanned: 32`, even though the control-plane record correctly identified token exhaustion.

Earlier HTTP 422, three call-deadline errors and HTTP 429 are separate observed invocation failures. The report does not attribute those to cancellation or assume that `auto` actually forced a particular provider thinking mode.

**Current code path**

1. `EvolveOrchestrator.checkSpendBudget()` checks after cost events; `tripBudget()` records the reason locally and calls `stop()`.
2. `completion_for().complete()` returns an empty string on cancellation without reporting a distinct cancellation result through its failure callback. `_model_call()` then calls `_Reporter.note_empty()`, so cancelled work can be labelled as a model's empty answer.
3. `script_domain.evaluate()` translates `RunStopped` into `valid=False` and `the search was stopped`. The reporter currently merges such nodes under `candidate-failed`.
4. `_Reporter.finish()` attempts held-out evaluation for any status other than `failed`, including `stopped`. That evaluation uses the same stopped callback, then the reporter emits “best candidate failed” for its cancellation result.

**Minimal reproduction of the cancellation/empty-result ambiguity**

Run from the repository root with Python 3.12+; only the standard library and repository source are used. The HTTP call is mocked, with no provider credentials or external requests:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=services/evolve/src python3 repro_cancel.py
```

```python
import io
import json
import threading
import uuid
from unittest.mock import patch
from sciencediscovery_evolve.completion import completion_for

stopped = threading.Event()
release = threading.Event()
finished = threading.Event()
failures = []

def fake_urlopen(*args, **kwargs):
    stopped.set()
    release.wait(2)
    finished.set()
    return io.BytesIO(json.dumps({'choices': [{'message': {'content': 'fixture'}}]}).encode())

complete = completion_for(
    'http://fixture.invalid/completions', uuid.uuid4().hex,
    should_stop=stopped.is_set, timeout=3,
)
with patch('urllib.request.urlopen', fake_urlopen):
    try:
        reply = complete('fixture', on_failure=failures.append)
        print({'reply': reply, 'failure_callbacks': failures, 'stopped': stopped.is_set()})
    finally:
        release.set()
        finished.wait(2)

```

Observed locally:

```text
{'reply': '', 'failure_callbacks': [], 'stopped': True}
```

For the finalization regression, use a fake domain whose `evaluate()` returns `(False, {"score": float("-inf")}, "the search was stopped")` when stopped, seed a valid best node, and invoke the reporter's stopped finalization with nonempty test shards. The current branch emits the misleading test-failure warning. This regression setup was identified by source inspection; it was not separately executed.

**Expected behavior / acceptance**

- Preserve cancellation and its cause across completion, candidate evaluation and terminal events. Cancelled calls must not claim that the model returned an empty answer; unevaluated candidates must be distinguishable from invalid programs.
- Treat search-budget exhaustion separately from final evaluation. For token exhaustion, provide a bounded finalization policy so the already-generated best candidate can be tested without further generation. If final testing cannot run, explicitly report it as cancelled/not evaluated and retain the reason. A user stop or hard wall-clock limit must remain promptly stoppable.
- Do not emit “best candidate failed” unless evaluation actually found a candidate failure.
- Preserve the true terminal cause rather than substituting `max_iters` for token exhaustion.
- Cover cancellation during completion, cancellation during candidate evaluation, token exhaustion before held-out evaluation, explicit user stop, and a genuine model empty answer with focused regressions.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Run configuration and outcome are quoted from the original `run.json`, complete `events.ndjson`, service log and frozen evaluator. Exact Windows build, hardware and installed Python patch version were not recorded in these artifacts; this report does not infer them.
- The small mocked cancellation reproduction above was executed successfully with `python3` in the Linux/WSL checkout. No full suite or new live model run was performed.

### Additional Information

1436.body:
### 🚀 Background Description

The desktop Evolve entry point lets a user choose PUCT/OpenEvolve and optionally provide a JSON candidate plus editable fields, but it has no dedicated controls for the search's total token budget, wall-clock budget or expansion budget. The run panel displays token/time consumption only after a run exists.

This prevents a user from directly choosing and verifying a bounded experiment before starting it. In a Windows PUCT run on 2026-11-26, the frozen run used 32 expansions, 4 workers, 600,000 total tokens and 7,200 seconds. These values could be inspected in the run record, but not configured in a desktop budget form.

Current source behavior:

- `DirectionDialog` confirms only the algorithm and optional candidate JSON/edit scope. Custom JSON fields belong to the candidate being evolved; adding a field named `maxTokens` there is not a search-budget setting.
- `BudgetBar` renders progress bars with no budget editor.
- `EvolveRunProposal` / `create_evolve_run` accept `expansions` and `workers`, so an agent can request them through conversation. They do not expose configurable total tokens or total seconds.
- `startProposedRun()` sets total tokens to 600,000 and total seconds to 7,200 using backend constants. The per-call ceiling is derived from algorithm/effective thinking mode.

Related: #1346 addresses range/interaction hints in the existing custom-parameter editor; #780 made the conversational checkpoint disclose a budget plan. This request is for an actual search-budget configuration surface and end-to-end parameter support, not another candidate JSON field or a prose-only plan.

### Design Ideas

Add a clearly labelled search-budget section to the Evolve setup/confirmation flow, separate from the candidate JSON editor:

- Total token cap, with units and validated bounds.
- Total elapsed-time cap, entered in minutes and stored in seconds.
- Maximum candidate expansions, labelled as expansions rather than an ambiguous total node count; state whether the baseline is excluded.
- An optional advanced concurrency setting, with the effective value shown before starting.
- Show the effective per-call token ceiling derived from the selected algorithm and thinking mode. At minimum this should be visible; if manual override is supported, validate it against existing model/algorithm constraints instead of silently changing it.

Display requested and effective values before confirmation, including limitations and concurrency-related budget exposure. Preserve current defaults for clients that omit overrides. Reject invalid values with field-specific messages, and explain any cross-field restriction before the run is created.

A minimal first implementation can be per-run; global defaults/session overrides are not required for this request. Keep the same budget readable in the frozen run and existing usage panel.

### Involved Public APIs

Extend the typed run proposal/tool and server validation with optional budget overrides, including total tokens and total seconds. Thread the confirmed values from the desktop submission through agent/tool invocation into the frozen `EvolveGoal.budget`; do not rely only on prompt wording for user-selected limits. Update `get_evolve_budget`/budget-plan calculation to describe those same effective limits. Existing clients and stored runs must remain compatible.

Do not add a write-only UI whose values are ignored by `proposal.ts` or permit arbitrary candidate JSON fields to override execution policy.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `apps/web`: Evolve setup/confirmation, submission state and API types, localized validation copy, current budget display. The Electron shell loads this UI.
- `packages/schema`, `packages/evolve`: proposal/budget types and tool contracts.
- `services/api`: proposal validation, shared budget plan, preflight, persistence and orchestrator enforcement.
- Both PUCT and OpenEvolve share the budget contract; defaults for either algorithm must remain valid.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Focused UI checks: enter valid limits and see effective values before confirmation; reject zero, negative, nonfinite, malformed and out-of-range values; preserve edits when navigating the setup flow; verify keyboard access and English/Chinese labels.
- A submission-to-persisted-run integration check: user-selected limits equal the tool request, effective plan and saved run budget; omitted overrides retain current defaults.
- Verify per-call ceilings and concurrency/expansion constraints with the same validation used by preflight. Do not silently coerce incompatible values.
- Add focused API/tool tests for new optional fields and backward compatibility; run typechecks for the affected packages.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Before starting an Evolve run, desktop users can set total tokens, total duration and maximum expansions in dedicated controls with units and bounds.
- [ ] Candidate JSON/edit scope is visibly separate from search configuration.
- [ ] Confirmation displays the effective budget and derived per-call token ceiling; invalid combinations cannot silently start with different limits.
- [ ] The user's confirmed limits reach the stored run and enforcement path without being replaced by backend constants or an agent's unrelated choice.
- [ ] Omitted overrides preserve current defaults and existing runs still load.
- [ ] Targeted UI/API/tool tests and affected package typechecks pass. Relevant typecheck commands include `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck`, and `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/evolve typecheck`.

### Additional Information

This request was established by inspecting the desktop/web implementation and backend proposal path; no new desktop/browser journey was run for this report. Budget-exhaustion finalization and cancellation diagnostics are tracked separately in #1435.

Checked against local `36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89` and fetched upstream main `3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1`; the relevant setup, budget display and proposal budget defaults remain unchanged.

- [Evolve confirmation dialog](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/apps/web/src/evolve/DirectionDialog.tsx#L41-L56)
- [Read-only budget display](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/apps/web/src/evolve/BudgetBar.tsx#L40-L65)
- [Backend budget defaults](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/services/api/src/evolution/call-budget.ts#L60-L70)
- [Frozen proposal budget](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/services/api/src/evolution/proposal.ts#L563-L575)

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched related issues; the evaluator-validation gap below is distinct from #1435 and #1436.
- [x] The relevant generation guidance and validation paths remain present in the latest upstream main inspected below.
- [x] Environment, a self-contained reproduction and the distinction between observed facts and proposed improvements are included.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

A generated `custom_script` evaluator can pass the current preparation/probe workflow while failing to enforce its own per-call runtime contract or protect scoring inputs. The immediate defects are in an experiment-generated script, not a checked-in scheduling evaluator. The repository-level defect is that the generation/validation workflow gives insufficient coverage of these failure modes before freezing the script and spending the search budget.

**Observed experiment and attribution**

A Windows desktop PUCT scheduling experiment on 2026-11-26 used `schedule(workloads, speeds) -> list[int]`, with a one-second per-call limit. Its frozen evaluator generated instances, recomputed an independent LPT baseline, validated assignments and scored `baseline_makespan / (baseline_makespan + candidate_makespan)`.

The original conversation records the design agent replacing SIGALRM with a daemon thread plus Queue watchdog for Windows compatibility, then validating the change with the fast LPT baseline and declaring it hardened. The resulting implementation uses `Queue.get(timeout=1)` but never terminates the timed-out thread. Three scored candidates later contained per-instance timeout errors. The frozen code establishes that work can continue after timeout; the historical logs do not quantify how much residual thread contention affected subsequent scores.

A separate direct check against that actual frozen evaluator confirmed an input-integrity defect: a synthetic candidate that replaces the received workload list with zeros and returns legal machine indices receives `score: 1.0`, with an empty error. Baseline makespan is calculated before candidate execution, while candidate makespan is calculated afterward from the same mutable objects. There is no evidence that the experiment's winning candidate exploited this defect.

**Why the current preparation/probe can miss it**

- The local Step 2 check in `skills/evolve-design/SKILL.md` explicitly checks only that the baseline executes and emits a number, delegating damaged-candidate checks to the server.
- `references/custom-script.md` specifies result/shard contracts and exception diagnostics, but not a reliable per-call timeout primitive or immutable scoring inputs.
- `proposal.ts:checkEvaluator()` checks script presence, size and required environment-variable markers. Runtime correctness is left to the probe.
- The `custom_script` probe tests the baseline, a hollowed-out candidate, unimportable candidates and baseline repeatability. It does not inject a slow/nonterminating entrypoint or an input-mutating entrypoint, or verify that work stops after the per-case timeout.
- The outer evaluator process has a killable timeout, but that does not enforce each individual call's deadline or prevent timed-out threads from affecting later cases inside that evaluator process.
- Repeating the fast baseline cannot establish timing stability of later near-deadline candidates. The current noise comparison uses the baseline-versus-damaged score gap, not the smaller improvement scale being measured.

The direct implementation mistake and the validation gap should both be addressed. Asking the model to be more careful does not establish the behavior.

**Self-contained reduced reproductions**

Save as `repro_evaluator.py` and run `python repro_evaluator.py`. Only the Python standard library is needed. This reproduces the relevant generated-script semantics, not a claim that a scheduling evaluator is built into the repository. The input-mutating case was also executed against the original frozen evaluator, with the same perfect score.

```python
import queue
import threading

# Reduced from the frozen evaluator: the baseline is measured before the call,
# but candidate makespan is computed from the same mutable input afterward.
def baseline_schedule(workloads, speeds):
    loads = [0.0] * len(speeds)
    assignment = [0] * len(workloads)
    for i in sorted(range(len(workloads)), key=workloads.__getitem__, reverse=True):
        j = min(range(len(speeds)), key=lambda j: loads[j] + workloads[i] / speeds[j])
        assignment[i] = j
        loads[j] += workloads[i] / speeds[j]
    return assignment

def makespan(workloads, speeds, assignment):
    loads = [0.0] * len(speeds)
    for i, w in enumerate(workloads):
        loads[assignment[i]] += w / speeds[assignment[i]]
    return max(loads)

def score_instance(schedule):
    workloads, speeds = [10.0, 8.0, 6.0], [1.0, 2.0]
    baseline = makespan(workloads, speeds, baseline_schedule(workloads, speeds))
    assignment = schedule(workloads, speeds)
    assert len(assignment) == len(workloads)
    assert all(type(j) is int and 0 <= j < len(speeds) for j in assignment)
    candidate = makespan(workloads, speeds, assignment)
    return baseline / (baseline + candidate)

def mutate_input(workloads, speeds):
    workloads[:] = [0.0] * len(workloads)
    return [0] * len(workloads)

print('baseline score:', score_instance(baseline_schedule))
print('input-mutating candidate score:', score_instance(mutate_input))

# The evaluator's thread/Queue watchdog stops waiting but not execution.
release, exited = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
q = queue.Queue()
def slow_candidate():
    try:
        release.wait()
        q.put('done')
    finally:
        exited.set()
worker = threading.Thread(target=slow_candidate, daemon=True)
worker.start()
try:
    q.get(timeout=0.01)  # Shortened from 1 second for this reproduction.
except queue.Empty:
    print('worker still alive after timeout:', worker.is_alive())
finally:
    release.set()
    worker.join(timeout=1)

```

Observed output from the reduced reproduction:

```text
baseline score: 0.5
input-mutating candidate score: 1.0
worker still alive after timeout: True
```

**Expected behavior and acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Provide a reusable, Windows-compatible candidate invocation facility for custom evaluators that need hard per-call limits. Deadline expiry must stop the corresponding work and clean up owned processes/resources before continuing; a daemon-thread wait timeout must not be represented as terminating execution. Define whether startup overhead counts toward the deadline.
- [ ] Keep authoritative scoring inputs/truth outside candidate-controlled mutation. A candidate may modify its own input copy, but this must not alter the data used to validate or calculate its result.
- [ ] Extend evaluator generation guidance and the pre-run checks with behavioral checks for slow/nonterminating calls, exceptions/invalid outputs, and input mutation where the evaluator's entrypoint protocol supports them. Test timeout followed by another valid case, so lingering work is observable. For arbitrary legacy scripts, use an explicit harness/protocol or disclose checks that cannot be performed rather than pretending generic Python is fully verified.
- [ ] Check repeatability of a time-constrained candidate under representative execution conditions, rather than validating timing only with a fast baseline. Preserve legitimate per-case zero penalties and partial scores; do not change every partially failing candidate into an invalid run.
- [ ] Add focused regressions for input-integrity and post-timeout cleanup on Windows and Linux; retain existing custom-script, shard, result and malformed-candidate compatibility checks.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Historical experiment: ScienceDiscovery Windows desktop, PUCT, direct/unisolated execution, four workers; generated instances had 50–300 tasks and 4–16 machines. Each scheduling call was limited to one second by the generated watchdog; the outer candidate/evaluator budget was 180 seconds.
- Evidence inspected: original conversation, frozen evaluator, run metadata, complete event stream and service log. Hardware, exact Windows build and installed Python patch version were not recorded in those artifacts and are not inferred here.
- The input-mutation check against the original evaluator and the reduced reproduction were executed in the Linux/WSL checkout using `python3`; no live search or full suite was rerun.

### Additional Information

- #1435 tracks budget-stop finalization/cancellation reporting, and #1436 tracks desktop budget controls. This issue concerns whether the generated measuring apparatus is reliable before search starts.
- The original evaluation score transform itself is not alleged to destroy flat-PUCT's ranking signal. However, a baseline of 0.5 is not evidence of useful optimization headroom. Task calibration against a known bound/reference is a separate useful improvement; it must not require solving the task during setup or weakening a user-requested baseline.
- Suggested implementation boundary: let the framework own execution/cleanup and input transport, while the model supplies task-specific instance generation, result validation and objective calculation. Preserve legacy scripts during migration rather than relying on a keyword ban on `threading`.

### Version Information

- The operator reports the experiment code matches the local checkout at `36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89`.
- Upstream main checked for this report: `3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1`. The affected generation guidance, custom-script probe and script-domain paths remain present.

- [Baseline-only local check](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/skills/evolve-design/SKILL.md#L163-L192)
- [Custom evaluator writing contract](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/skills/evolve-design/references/custom-script.md#L7-L30)
- [Custom-script discrimination probe](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/probe.py#L109-L178)
- [Baseline repeatability check](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/probe.py#L479-L508)
- [Outer evaluator execution](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/script_domain.py#L254-L300)

### Checklist

- [x] Searched related open issues; #668 tracks the external-runtime bridge, but does not cover the Desktop capability-selection and runtime-editing defects below.
- [ ] Verified against the latest release (this report is based on the source revision below).
- [x] Included source locations, minimal reproduction steps, environment, and validation scope.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

Desktop Settings can create MCP servers and Specialists, but the Specialist form does not consistently match execution behavior. Two source-confirmed defects affect capability selection and preservation of runtime settings; two related UI gaps expose incomplete external-runtime support as if it were available.

These findings come from tracing the form, persistence, session binding, and task execution paths. The reproduction steps below describe scenarios to verify; they have not been executed as browser/product journeys in this review.

#### 1. “Specific capabilities” does not restrict the Specialist to its selected capabilities

Steps:
1. Enable connectors A and B for the parent session.
2. Create a Native Specialist and choose only connector A under specific capabilities.
3. Bind the Specialist to a session, or dispatch a task to it.
4. Inspect the resulting tool catalog or attempt to use connector B.

Expected: B is unavailable, as the form explicitly promises that unselected capabilities remain invisible and uncallable even when globally enabled.

Source behavior: both session and child-task assembly union the Specialist lists with the parent/session lists. B remains in the effective connector set. Skills are also unioned. The stored schema has no separate capability-access mode, so choosing an empty specific list also serializes identically to full access.

Sources at the reviewed revision:
- [Form serialization](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/apps/desktop/src/views/settings/system/SpecialistForm.tsx#L117-L125)
- [UI capability promise](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts#L1677-L1687)
- [Session capability union](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/services/api/src/runs/index.ts#L3365-L3375)
- [Child-task capability union](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/services/api/src/runs/index.ts#L1905-L1912)

#### 2. Editing a Specialist drops advanced runtime options

Steps:
1. Configure an external Specialist with runtime options such as `fallback: false`, `timeoutSeconds`, `reasoningEffort`, or `execution` through the supported runtime configuration path.
2. Open that Specialist in Desktop Settings.
3. Change only its name or description and save.
4. Read the saved Specialist record.

Expected: unrelated runtime options survive the edit.

Source behavior: the draft retains only runtime kind and model, and `runtimeOf()` reconstructs the entire runtime object from those two fields. The update replaces the previous runtime object, removing all the other settings. In particular, losing `fallback: false` allows unavailable-runtime recovery again.

Sources:
- [Draft and runtime serialization](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/apps/desktop/src/views/settings/system/SpecialistForm.tsx#L94-L124)
- [Specialist update and normalization](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/services/api/src/store.ts#L4986-L4993)
- [Fallback decision](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/services/api/src/specialist-runtime/agent.ts#L86-L93)

#### 3. External-runtime Specialists can select capabilities that are not bridged to them

Create a Codex, Claude Code, or ACP Specialist and add an MCP connector or Skill. Dispatch an explicit `task(specialistId=...)` to that Specialist.

The external adapter receives only a fixed platform-tool allowlist. MCP tools and `read_skill` are filtered out, so saving the capability selection does not make those tools callable through the platform bridge.

This implementation gap is already tracked in #668. The Desktop-specific problem is that the new form offers the same capability configuration without explaining or restricting this unsupported combination. Either complete the bridge under #668 or make the supported combinations clear in the form.

Source: [External adapter tool filtering](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/services/api/src/specialist-runtime/agent.ts#L70-L78).

#### 4. Selecting an external-runtime Specialist in the composer does not explain explicit delegation

Create a Codex Specialist, select it in the session's expert picker, and send a message. Session binding applies its instructions to the main agent; it does not switch the main conversation to Codex. A child task that merely inherits the session Specialist also does not activate the external runtime without an explicit Specialist ID in the task input.

#668 intentionally requires explicit `task(specialistId=...)` targeting. This is a UI guidance gap, not a request to remove that contract: the picker/form should explain how to invoke the configured external runtime and distinguish session instruction binding from external task execution.

Sources:
- [Session Specialist binding](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/services/api/src/runs/index.ts#L2440-L2443)
- [Explicit runtime activation condition](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/services/api/src/runs/index.ts#L1697-L1704)

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Desktop React application and API service, source checkout on Linux/WSL2.
- Node.js v22.19.0; pnpm 11.1.2.
- The capability assembly and serialization findings do not depend on GPU hardware or a particular model provider.

### Additional Information

Validation performed:

```sh
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop exec tsx --import ./tests/support/css-preload.mjs --test tests/api-settings.test.ts tests/settings-pages.test.tsx
```

Result: 62 tests passed, 0 failed. These tests cover request construction and static page behavior, not the execution scenarios above. No service startup, browser/E2E journey, or live external-provider invocation was performed.

The MCP create/save/test/catalog path did not reveal a definite blocker during source review. Connection testing can succeed while the server remains disabled; actual use requires enabling the service and selecting the source in effective session settings. A passing connection test alone is not evidence that a Specialist can use it.

Suggested acceptance:
- Specific capability selection matches its UI promise in both session and delegated-task execution, including an empty selection.
- Editing unrelated Specialist fields preserves advanced runtime options.
- External-runtime capability limitations and explicit invocation requirements are accurately represented in Desktop until #668 supplies the missing bridge.
- Add targeted coverage for these boundaries and verify the corresponding Desktop journeys.

### Version Information

Reviewed source revision: `36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89`.

Related: #668 and #575.
